1.text: Bhagirathi originates at Gomukh in Uttarkashi district, Uttarakhand.
Alaknanda and Bhagirathi meet at Devprayag, Uttarakhand.
Alaknanda becomes the Ganga after meeting Bhagirathi at Devprayag.
Alaknanda originates at Satopanth Glacier above Badrinath.
Ganga enters the plains at Haridwar.
Ganga flows through Farakka in West Bengal before entering Bangladesh.
Ganga is known as Padma in Bangladesh.
Yamuna originates at Yamunotri Glacier on the western slopes of Banderpunch Peak.
Yamuna and Ganga meet at Prayagraj.
Chambal originates near Dr. Ambedkar Nagar (Mhow) in Madhya Pradesh.
Chambal flows through Sawai Madhopur and Dholpur in Rajasthan.
Chambal joins the Yamuna.
Gandak originates in the Nepal Himalayas.
Gandak joins the Ganga at Sonpur near Patna, Bihar.
Ghaghra originates at Mapchachungo Glacier.
Sharda joins Ghaghra in the plains.
Ghaghra meets the Ganga at Revilganj in Saran, Bihar.
Ramganga joins the Ganga near Kannauj, Uttar Pradesh.
Damodar originates at Khamarpat Hill on the Chota Nagpur Plateau.
Damodar flows through a rift valley to the Hugli.
Mahananda is the last left-bank tributary of the Ganga.
Mahananda joins the Ganga in West Bengal.
Son originates at Amarkantak Hill.
Son joins the Ganga near Patna, Bihar.
Brahmaputra flows through Tibet, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and Bangladesh.
Brahmaputra is called Tsangpo or Sanpu in Tibet.
Brahmaputra is called Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh.
Brahmaputra is called Brahmaputra in Assam.
Brahmaputra is called Jamuna in Bangladesh.
Dibang flows across Dibang Valley and Lower Dibang Valley districts in Arunachal Pradesh.
Kameng flows through Arunachal Pradesh and Assam.
Lohit originates in eastern Tibet.
Lohit flows through Arunachal Pradesh and Assam.
Subansiri originates in Tibet.
Subansiri flows through Arunachal Pradesh and Assam.
Manas is a tributary of the Brahmaputra.
Kopili, also called Kapili, is a tributary of the Brahmaputra.
Sankosh originates in northern Bhutan.
Sankosh joins the Brahmaputra near the Assam–West Bengal border.
Sankosh forms the boundary between Assam and West Bengal.
Teesta flows through Sikkim and West Bengal.
Teesta joins the Brahmaputra in Bangladesh.
Rangeet originates in Sikkim.
Rangeet is a tributary of the Teesta.
Majuli is a river island in the Brahmaputra in Assam.
Godavari originates at Nasik, also spelled Nashik, in Maharashtra.
Godavari flows from Nashik through Maharashtra, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.
Nanded is on the Godavari.
Nashik is on the Godavari.
Rajamahendravaram is on the Godavari.
The Godavari delta is on the eastern coast.
Krishna originates at Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra.
Vijayawada is on the Krishna.
Srisailam is on the Krishna.
Musi is a tributary of the Krishna.
Sihawa is the origin of the Mahanadi.
Cuttack is on the Mahanadi.
Kuakhai is part of the Mahanadi delta at Bhubaneswar.
Tiruchirappalli is on the Cauvery.
Shivasamudram is a waterfall on the Cauvery.
Narmada originates at Amarkantak in the Maikal Range.
Narmada Valley lies between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.
Jabalpur is on the Narmada.
Bhedaghat is on the Narmada.
Dhuandhar Falls is on the Narmada in Jabalpur district, Madhya Pradesh.
Kapildhara Falls is on the Narmada in Anuppur district, Madhya Pradesh.
Narmada flows west through a rift valley to the Arabian Sea.
Tapi, also called Tapti, originates at Multai in Betul district, Madhya Pradesh.
Multai is the origin of the Tapi.
Tapi is associated with Betul district in Madhya Pradesh.
Tapi has its source at Surat in Gujarat.
Tapi flows westward to the Arabian Sea.
Mahi originates in Madhya Pradesh.
Mahi enters Rajasthan at Banswara district.
Mahi flows through Gujarat.
Mahi flows southwestward.
Mahi empties into the Gulf of Khambhat.
Mahi crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice.
Jhelum originates at Verinag at the foot of the Pir Panjal.
Jhelum flows through Srinagar and Wular Lake.
Jhelum enters Pakistan through a deep and narrow gorge.
Kishanganga is a tributary of the Jhelum.
Kishanganga is called Neelum in Pakistan.
Ravi joins the Chenab in Pakistan.
Chenab receives the Jhelum and Ravi.
Sutlej receives the Chenab and joins the Indus.
Ludhiana and Firozpur are on the old bank of the Sutlej.
Leh lies on the right bank of the Indus.
Luni originates southwest of Ajmer in Rajasthan in the Aravalli region.
Luni flows through the southeastern Thar to the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.
Zanskar lies on the border of Himachal Pradesh and Ladakh near Sarchu.
Zanskar joins the Indus at Nimu.
Spiti originates at Kunzam La.
Spiti joins the Sutlej near Khab in Kinnaur district, Himachal Pradesh.
Kali rises near Diggi village in Uttara Kannada, Karnataka.
Kali flows westward to the Arabian Sea.
Hagari, also called Vedavathi, flows from the Western Ghats through Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh to the Tungabhadra.
Mithi originates at Vihar Lake in Mumbai.
Water from Powai Lake joins the Mithi.
Mithi flows to the Arabian Sea near the Bay of Mahim.
Sankosh flows from northern Bhutan to the Brahmaputra.
Sankosh forms the Assam–West Bengal boundary.
